html:
The Trio, or Tiriyó, who call themselves Tarëno, are a Cariban-speaking people of the forests on the border of southern Suriname and northern Brazil, around the Sipaliwini savanna and the Tumuc-Humac mountains.

They live by farming cassava in forest gardens, hunting and fishing, and they trade with neighbours such as the Wayana and with Maroon communities downriver. Until the mid 1900s they lived in small, scattered villages. In the 1960s missionaries and airstrips drew most Trio into larger settlements such as Kwamalasamutu in Suriname. Their language belongs to the Cariban family, like that of the Kalina of the coast.
